issues.legal_issue: A purchaser of only part of an undertaking’s assets, who was not its successor-in-interest and was not involved when the workers’ services were terminated or the dispute was referred, is not liable for the workers’ claims against the former management.
material_facts: The workers’ services were terminated by the Superintendent acting for a court-appointed Receiver before the purchaser acquired any interest in the tea gardens.
The dispute was referred to the Labour Court before the purchase, and the purchaser was not a party to the reference when it was made.

The purchaser acquired only the equity of redemption in part of the company’s assets, subject to the mortgage decree and related liabilities, and did not acquire the company’s goodwill or take over its liabilities.
The workers did not establish that the transfer met the conditions for the statutory exception applicable to a transfer of an undertaking.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was not liable for the workers’ claims, and the workers could not obtain reinstatement against it.
issues.legal_principle: Applying sections 25F and 25FF of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and the principles in Anakapalla Co-operative Agricultural and Industrial Society Ltd. v. Workmen, the Court held that the purchaser was not a successor-in-interest on the facts of the sale. Even assuming ownership of the undertaking had been transferred, the workers’ claims were to be considered against the former company under section 25FF, because the proviso to that section was not shown to apply.

rule.if: industrial_dispute_reference and termination_preceded_purchase and purchaser_acquired_limited_assets_without_goodwill and transfer_exception_conditions_absent

predicates.industrial_dispute_reference: A government referred a dispute concerning workers’ employment to a labour adjudicator.
predicates.termination_preceded_purchase: The workers’ services were terminated before the purchaser acquired an interest in the undertaking.
predicates.purchaser_acquired_limited_assets_withou: The purchaser acquired only limited assets and did not acquire the undertaking’s goodwill or assume the former management’s liabilities.
predicates.transfer_exception_conditions_absent: The transfer was not shown to meet the conditions that would bring it within the exception to the ordinary rule governing transferred undertakings.

issues.definition: When an employment dispute is referred after workers have been terminated, a purchaser who acquired only limited assets without goodwill and whose transfer does not meet the exception conditions is not liable for those pre-transfer claims.

issues.legal_issue: A Labour Court cannot treat a reference as infructuous merely because the incoming purchaser is not liable; it must bring the Receiver, the liquidator, or both before it and consider the workers’ claims.
material_facts: The reference concerned whether the termination of fifteen workers’ services was justified and whether they were entitled to reinstatement or other relief.
The Receiver had managed the tea gardens when the workers’ services were terminated, and the company was in liquidation under an Official Liquidator.
The incoming purchaser was not liable for the workers’ claims, but the Labour Court had not brought the Receiver or the Official Liquidator before it to adjudicate those claims.
The Labour Court instead closed the proceedings on the ground that the reference had become infructuous.
issues.conclusion: The Labour Court should have issued notice to the Receiver, the Official Liquidator, or both, and adjudicated the workers’ entitlement to relief in their presence; the award was set aside and the reference remitted for fresh consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, contemplates that parties summoned by the Labour Court may be made parties to the proceedings and bound by the award. The terms of the reference gave the Labour Court jurisdiction to determine whether the termination was justified and whether reinstatement or other relief was due. The Court held that the proceedings could not simply be closed after rejecting the claim against the purchaser.

predicates.industrial_dispute_reference: A government referred a dispute concerning workers’ employment to a labour adjudicator.
predicates.incoming_purchaser_not_liable: The incoming purchaser was found not liable for the workers’ claims.
predicates.receiver_or_liquidator_not_before_labour: The Receiver or liquidator responsible for representing the former employer’s estate had not been brought before the Labour Court to address the workers’ claims.

issues.definition: If a purchaser is not liable in a referred employment dispute and the former employer’s estate representatives are not before the Labour Court, the court must bring the relevant representatives before it and adjudicate the workers’ claims.

issues.legal_issue: Whether the workers’ claims are governed by the rules for retrenchment or for transfer of an undertaking depends on the basis of the claims.
material_facts: The workers’ services were terminated while a Receiver managed the tea gardens, and the purchaser acquired an interest in the gardens afterward.

The Court directed the Labour Court to reconsider the workers’ claims against the appropriate parties and distinguished between a claim that services had been dispensed with by way of retrenchment and a claim based on a transfer of the undertaking.
issues.conclusion: On reconsideration, the Labour Court must determine the claims under the rules applicable to their asserted basis: retrenchment or transfer of the undertaking.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed that a claim based on retrenchment be adjudicated under section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and a claim based on a transfer of the undertaking be adjudicated under section 25FF of that Act.

predicates.industrial_dispute_reference: A government referred a dispute concerning workers’ employment to a labour adjudicator.
predicates.claim_based_on_retrenchment: The workers assert that their services were dispensed with by way of retrenchment.
predicates.claim_based_on_undertaking_transfer: The workers base their claim on a transfer of the undertaking.

issues.definition: In a referred employment dispute, the asserted basis of the workers’ claim determines which legal regime governs its adjudication.
